title: Orbit and Vector
premise: Lena Dunmore, a veteran insurance investigator who ferries claims along the silent trade routes between quarantined worlds, is the only witness to the Nine-Second Flicker, when gravity failed system-wide and something erased an entire mining colony from every record. Pursued by the Consortium's adjusters who insist no massacre ever occurred, Lena follows a trail of corrupted memory cores to the derelict reactor station Kepler's Rest, where the flicker originated as a cover for genocide disguised as an accident. As the reactor counts down toward a second, permanent erasure—one that will take his own memories with it—Lena must choose between broadcasting the truth and saving the last living witness: his estranged sister, whose implanted memories hold the only proof. He sacrifices his recollection of her to preserve hers, sending the evidence out on the long route while remaining a man who can never remember why it mattered.
about_author: Quentin Eriksen is a former maritime salvage auditor who spent eleven years inspecting wrecks before turning to fiction. He writes slow-burn space mysteries from a converted trawler off the Norwegian coast.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: POV Lena. Establishing his solitary life hauling insurance claims between worlds that severed contact after the Accord War; he prides himself on seeing everything and recording nothing. Emotional beat: comfortable loneliness about to shatter.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: POV Lena. Gravity fails across the entire system for exactly nine seconds; in the chaos, Lena glimpses a colony ship's distress burst from Meridian Station—a station official records say was decommissioned decades ago. Beat: dread and curiosity overriding self-preservation.

chapters.title: Claims Against Nothing
chapters.summary: POV Lena. At Ceres Registry he files an inquiry into Meridian and finds its entire history scrubbed—permits, deaths, even his own past claim visit. A Consortium adjuster named Voss politely suggests he drop it. Beat: gaslit unease hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Dead Kept
chapters.summary: POV Lena, with interludes from a damaged memory core. On a scavver hulk he recovers corrupted cores from Meridian survivors, including one bearing his sister Mara's voiceprint—Mara, who vanished twenty years ago. Beat: grief reopened as motive.

chapters.title: The Adjuster's Smile
chapters.summary: POV Voss. The antagonist chapter: Voss reports to Consortium handlers that Dunmore is becoming a liability; we learn the flicker was a weapon test and Meridian's population the price. Beat: cold institutional menace, loyalty to the firm over truth.

chapters.title: Kepler's Rest
chapters.summary: POV Lena. Following core coordinates, Lena reaches the derelict reactor station where the flicker originated—and finds it occupied by a half-mad caretaker AI still logging the massacre in real time. Beat: horror and awe as the scale of the crime becomes undeniable.

chapters.title: Countdown
chapters.summary: POV Lena. The reactor is armed for a second pulse designed to erase residual evidence—including the AI and anyone aboard. Voss arrives with enforcers; Lena bargains using the one thing they want: the cores. Beat: cornered desperation sharpening into strategy.

chapters.title: Sister, Stranger
chapters.summary: POV alternating Lena/Mara. Mara arrives alive but memory-wiped, her implanted mind the only intact record of Meridian. Extracting the proof will destroy what remains of her—or him. Beat: the loyalty-versus-truth theme made flesh.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV Lena. Climax: under fire, Lena uploads the massacre record onto the long route's relay network while triggering the reactor early, sacrificing the station and his own stored memories of Mara to shield her extraction. Beat: triumphant, devastating sacrifice.

chapters.title: Vector Home
chapters.summary: POV Mara, closing on Lena. Weeks later, the truth spreads system-wide; Consortium adjusters fall. Mara finds Lena running the long route again, not knowing why she cries when she sees him. She books passage anyway. Beat: bittersweet resolution—truth survives, memory doesn't have to be whole to be enough.
